notes:
User struggles with falling asleep and sleep quality despite journaling and a consistent sleep schedule. They use yoga and meditation for self-care and anxiety relief. They now see Dr. Smith weekly and find the sessions helpful for workload, anxiety, and healthy-boundary work.

User feels overwhelmed by work and social commitments, especially difficulty saying no to colleagues and friends. Their top priority is meeting work deadlines without burnout. They work 9–5 Monday–Friday, attend weekly yoga, and have a biweekly dinner with friends. They want to preserve time for meditation, journaling, relaxation, and flexibility rather than follow a rigid schedule.

They plan to use a simple flexible checklist: each day identify 3–5 must-dos, make time for self-care, decline nonessential commitments, communicate priorities, and leave buffer time. Weekly, they will review priorities and commitments, adjust as needed, and reflect on self-care and progress. They especially value the weekly review and feel more confident setting boundaries, including limiting social commitments. They plan to discuss boundary plans with Dr. Smith, use calm, non-blaming communication, listen and offer compromises
trajectory:
User struggles with falling asleep and sleep quality despite journaling and a consistent sleep schedule. They use yoga and meditation as self-care, which has helped their anxiety, and wonder whether these also support sleep. They have therapy every two weeks with Dr. Smith and look forward to discussing progress.

User has felt overwhelmed by commitments. Dr. Smith encouraged them to learn to say “no” and set healthy boundaries. They want to limit social commitments with their partner because they sometimes prefer staying home to relax, while their partner frequently invites them to events. They believe healthy boundaries are appropriate in the relationship.

User plans to calmly discuss social-event boundaries with their partner using “I” statements, anticipate concerns or resistance, listen thoughtfully, stay calm and assertive, offer compromises/alternatives, reaffirm that boundaries support a balanced relationship, and avoid blaming language. Potential pushback may involve fears of changing relationship rules, reduced fun, or abandonment. They appreciate practical, reassuring guidance and are ready to take this step.
